deep_dive.title: Refining Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation via Regional Semantics and Visual Prototypes
deep_dive.abstract: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) has shown superior performance in the image-level open-vocabulary classification task, benefiting from its powerful alignment of visual features and text embeddings. However, dense prediction tasks require models to perform pixel-level predictions, necessitating modifications to CLIP for region-text alignment. In this paper, we adjust the attention layers within the vanilla visual encoder of CLIP. With a novel attention calculation method for selective attention features, the model retains more regional semantic information. To further mitigate the negative impact of the modality gap, we introduce additional visual prototypes to refine the original predictor solely based on text embeddings. Specifically, patch features with confident predictions are selected to form an additional auxiliary memory-based classifier for more accurate prediction. We further integrate an optimizable feature extractor with an exponential moving average updating strategy to enhance prediction quality. Extensive experiments on $5$ semantic segmentation datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: Improves CLIP-based dense prediction by adjusting attention layers to retain regional semantics and adding visual prototypes to refine the text-only predictor, mitigating the modality gap for open-vocabulary segmentation.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 针对CLIP在图像级分类上表现优异、但用于像素级密集预测时区域与文本对齐不足的问题，该文调整CLIP视觉编码器的注意力层，提出选择性注意力特征的新计算方式以保留更多区域语义信息。为缓解模态鸿沟带来的负面影响，作者额外引入视觉原型来修正仅依赖文本嵌入的预测器。实验表明该方法在开放词汇语义分割任务上提升了区域级判别与分割质量，为视觉语言模型向密集预测迁移提供了可行改进路径。

quick_skim.title: OV-Foam: How 3D Representations Shape Semantic Feature Lifting
quick_skim.abstract: Existing feature lifting approaches for open-vocabulary segmentation rely on simple backprojection to assign features to primitives. In the case of 3D Gaussian splatting reconstruction, the primitives overlap heavily, leading to suboptimal reconstructions, governed by many primitives per ray. Backprojection, however, reduces to a least-squares solvable problem, exactly when no two primitives share a ray. Motivated by this insight, we propose OV-Foam, which uses PowerFoam as the underlying representation. This representation uses a power-diagram to partition the scene, resulting in zero overlap between primitives and a substantial reduction in primitives per ray, which ultimately simplifies the lifting problem and allows for closer-to-optimal feature assignment. We show that the space partitioning primitives of OV-Foam reach near-optimal assignment, and our experiments demonstrate improved open-vocabulary segmentation over Gaussian baselines.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Shows that backprojection-based feature lifting for open-vocabulary segmentation is ill-posed when primitives overlap, and proposes OV-Foam using a power-diagram representation with zero overlap to obtain closer-to-optimal feature assignment.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 针对开放词汇分割中特征提升依赖简单反投影、而在三维高斯泼溅基元严重重叠时该问题退化为不适定最小二乘的问题，该文指出只有当射线不共享两个基元时反投影才可解。为此提出OV-Foam，采用PowerFoam幂图划分场景，使基元之间零重叠并大幅减少每条射线上的基元数量，从而简化特征提升并得到更接近最优的特征分配。实验分析了不同三维表示对语义特征提升效果的影响。
